title: Old-Time Onion Storage
subtitle: Tips From a 1939 Farm Bulletin
items: Cure in shade until they rattle
desc: Old-time onion storage tips from a 1939 USDA cooperative farm bulletin: harvest when the tops fall over, cure in the shade until the skins rattle, use thick-necked bulbs first, and keep onions cool, dry and well ventilated in open crates all winter.

title: How to Can Pears
subtitle: USDA Water Bath Method
desc: How to can pear halves safely in a boiling water bath, following the USDA Complete Guide to Home Canning: hot pack in light syrup or juice, 1/2-inch headspace, 20 minutes for pints and 25 for quarts at 0–1,000 ft, with longer times at higher altitudes.

title: How to Dry Fresh Herbs
subtitle: Easy Homestead Pantry Skill
items: Hang in a dark, airy spot
desc: How to dry fresh herbs at home: harvest in the morning before plants flower, hang small bunches in a dark, airy spot (or use a dehydrator at 95–115°F) until crumbly, then store whole leaves airtight away from light for a flavorful winter pantry.

title: Power Outage Kit Checklist
subtitle: Be Ready Before the Storm
desc: Build a power outage emergency kit before winter storms hit: flashlights with spare batteries, a battery or hand-crank radio, a manual can opener, a charged power bank, a first aid kit with medicines, and some cash. Simple off grid preparedness.

title: Put Your Garden to Bed
subtitle: Fall Cleanup for Better Soil
desc: How to put your vegetable garden to bed in fall: pull spent crops, throw out diseased plants instead of composting them, cover beds with compost, shredded leaves or mulch, and clean your tools for a healthier garden next spring.
